extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) preparing for or conducting patent prosecution interviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for requesting, preparing for, conducting, and following up on examiner interviews during patent prosecution, including use of the USPTO Automated Interview Request (AIR) form, timing/options, roles, and allowable/denial reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits of interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews during patent prosecution provide an opportunity for the participants to discuss the merits of an application and gain insights that are sometimes not apparent through written exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefits include improved communication, understanding trends, and various interview options; interviews can resolve issues and shorten prosecution (Director’s forum quote and slide noting percent of serial disposals having interviews).

rubrics_metrics.name: When an interview should be granted (MPEP 713 standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: “An interview should be granted when the nature of the case is such that the interview serves to develop and clarify outstanding issues in an application and leads to a mutual understanding between the examiner and the applicant, and thereby advance the prosecution of the application.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this MPEP 713 test as the controlling policy: grant interviews that develop/clarify outstanding issues and advance prosecution. Interviews are an effective tool to resolve issues and shorten prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview timing/options
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible interview timing/options include: Filing, First action, After final, Allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the interview timing appropriate to the prosecution stage; interviews can occur at multiple stages (e.g., pre-first action or after final action) depending on the issues to be resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated Interview Request (AIR) form — purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: An Automated Interview Request (AIR) form is an alternative way for applicant to initially request an interview with examiner using a convenient online form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The AIR form is a mechanism to initiate the conversation to schedule an interview, similar to an applicant leaving a voicemail. The examiner is expected to follow up on the request within one (1) business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: AUTOMATED INTERVIEW REQUEST (AIR) form — location and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The AIR form is found on the external USPTO website at www.uspto.gov/interviewpractice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are made aware of the availability of the AIR form in the conclusion paragraph of an Office action; provide the web link to the AIR form when directing applicants to request interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant AIR email confirmation contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant receives an email that contains confirmation that AIR form was submitted and clarifications about next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirmation email should: clarify applicant next step(s) for submitting written authorization if needed; clarify that written authorization cannot be accepted via email; clarify that the examiner still has to grant/deny interview in accordance with USPTO policy; encourage applicant to contact examiner within two (2) business days if no communication was received from examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner AIR email confirmation contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner receives an email confirmation which includes application number and applicant contact information, date/time of interview (and alternates), topic(s) for discussion, and a reminder to contact applicant within one (1) business day to confirm the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examiner confirmation to ensure scheduling details and topics are clear and to prompt timely examiner contact within one business day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner AIR confirmation — next steps and escalation guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner confirmation email clarifies next steps for examiner including applicant’s written authorization selection, reminds examiner to contact SPE if interview is denied, and provides a Quick Reference Guide (QRG) and contact info for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the clarified next steps (e.g., handle written authorization per selection), escalate to SPE when denying interviews as required, and consult provided QRG/contact info if assistance needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons interviews are denied
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews are denied when: (1) an appeal brief has been filed in the application; (2) the requestor has no authorization to act on applicant's behalf; (3) the interview is not prearranged (e.g., attorney/applicant shows up without prior notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify authorization and case status before scheduling; do not grant unarranged walk-in interviews; if denying, follow policy and notify appropriate supervisors (SPE) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant preparation for the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should prepare a detailed agenda that clearly states the objective in advance, explain the inventive concept and any differences to distinguish patentability, and discuss how the inventive concept is captured in the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, applicant should propose a response or an amendment to the claims; providing a focused agenda and proposed claim language improves efficiency and the likelihood of resolving issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparation for the interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner should review the proposed agenda prior to the interview and be prepared to explain how the applied prior art is interpreted and how the art reads on the claim limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify areas of agreement and allowable subject matter for a focused meeting; identify additional resources for effective discourse; strive to resolve differences during the interview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview participants and immediate goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties present: Applicant: power of attorney (POA). USPTO: an examiner with negotiation authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the interview, identify common ground and resolve outstanding issues; ensure participants have appropriate authority and representation to discuss and make prosecution decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-interview follow-up procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner sends to applicants an Interview Summary stating the substance of the interview (PTOL-413); applicant sends to the examiner a summary of the interview; next steps for prosecution are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both parties should exchange post-interview summaries to record substance and agreed next steps; use PTOL-413 for examiner summary to ensure consistent documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources for interview practice and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Available resources include: AIR Training Guide; Interview Practice USPTO Webpage; USPTO Automated Interview Request (AIR) Form; MPEP Reference for Interviews; TC Interview Specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult these resources and training materials for guidance on interview policy, use of AIR, practice tips, and contacts for support.
